texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) arises out of a road accident that occurred on 19.10.2017, in which the petitioner Ekta (aged about 5 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury and amputation of first and second tow of her right foot. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 19.10.2017 at around 9:30 am, the petitioner, who was playing behind a parked car was was hit by a car bearing registration no. DL2C-AT-4420 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) while the petitioner was trying to cross the road. Petitioner was taken to Safdarjung Hospital by driver of the offending vehicle, where she was treated and two toes of her right foot were amputated. 3. An FIR No.220 of 2017 dated 19.10.2017 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC at PS Defence Colony and the matter was investigated. After investigation, a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner of offending vehicle and Respondent no.3 is the Insurance Company with which such offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident. 5. In response to the claim, Respondent no.1 & 2 filed their reply denying negligence of respondent no.1. It has been pleaded that Respondent no.1 was neither rash nor negligent while Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.08.08 17:27:17 +0530 MACT NO: 510/18 EKTA VS. PIDAPARTHI P.No 2 of 24 BK driving the offending vehicle and could not have foreseen the victim coming out from behind a parked vehicle all of a sudden. It has been pleaded that the accident occurred due to negligence of the minor victim who was trying to cross the road unattended by any adult. Respondent no.2 has not denied to be the owner of the offending vehicle and pleaded that the vehicle was duly insured by Respondent no.3. Respondent no. 3 has also denied its liability to compensate the petitioner. It has been pleaded in the reply that since the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner and there is a delay of 37 days in registration of FIR, petitioner is not entitled to compensation. 6. On the basis of pleadings on record, following issues were framed on 07.05.2018:- 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 19.10.2017 due to Ekta (Dar) vs Pidaparthi (220/17 Dfc) on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77060891/ 2 rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL2CAT4420 being driven by R1 and owned by R2? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. In order to prove its case, petitioner no.1 Ganga Dayal Pal, examined himself as PW-1 and Sh. Madan Gopal (eye witness), examined as PW-2. PW-1/Gagan Dayal tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he deposed that on 19.10.2017 at about 9:30am, his daughter namely Ekta aged about 5 years, was standing in front of her residence i.e. at Road Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.08 17:27:23 +0530 MACT NO: 510/18 EKTA VS. PIDAPARTHI P.No 3 of 24 BK no. 7, in front of quarter no. 7/1555, Andrewj Ganj, New Delhi. At that time, all of sudden one vehicle bearing no. DL2CAT4420 (CAR) came at a high speed which was driven by the driver/Respondent no. 1(who was a lady driver) in rash and negligent manner and in contravention of rules of traffic and hit the petitioner/minor/my daughter with very great force. Due to this, the petitioner/injured/minor fell on the road and the offending vehicle run over and crushed the foot of his daughter. She sustained multiple grievous injuries and first and second toe of her right leg were amputated. She also sustained fracture of the proximal portion of her right leg. PW-1 relied upon MLC of the petitioner as Ex.PW1/1, Discharge summary as Ex.PW1/2, Medical prescription and other treatment papers as Ex.PW1/3, Medical Bills as Ex.PW1/4, Aadhar Card of the petitioner as Ex.PW1/5, Aadhar Card of PW1 as Ex.PW1/6 and copy of DAR as Ex.PW1/7. PW-1 was duly cross examined by respondent no.3. PW2/Madan Gopal (eye witness) deposed as an eye witness. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW2/A. He depose that on 19.10.2017, at about 9:30am he was sitting on the side of the road when a car bearing Reg. No. DL2CAT4420 came from Ring Road side on Road no. 7 and drove towards Road no. 3. At that time, petitioner, aged about 5 years, was playing near a vehicle that was parked alongside the road. When the petitioner was crossing the road, offending vehicle which was driven by a lady, at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, ran over the leg of the petitioner. At that time, Smt. Srivati, mother of the petitioner came to the spot. The CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.08 17:27:31 +0530 MACT NO: 510/18 EKTA VS. PIDAPARTHI P.No 4 of 24 BK driver of the offending vehicle stopped her car and took the injured accompanied by her mother, to the hospital. He deposed that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of Respondent no.1. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-2/A. He was duly cross-examined by learned counsel for Respondent no.3. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: On the other hand, it has been contended on behalf of insurance company that since even the eye witness has testified that the offending vehicle was at normal speed, the sole negligence of the petitioner becomes apparent. It is further argued that there is a delay of 37 days in lodging of the FIR and even as per the chargesheet, IO has not arrived at a conclusion that Respondent no.1 was rash or negligent in driving the offending vehicle. 10. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as (2009 ACJ 287), that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 14. The driver of the offending vehicle has not entered the witness box or raised any defence to negate or refute the allegations of rash and negligent driving. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.08 17:28:07 +0530 MACT NO: 510/18 EKTA VS. PIDAPARTHI P.No 9 of 24 BK consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 18. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 18.1 In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 18.2 It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 18.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 18.5.
